name: MedusaJS-Storefront
description: The Next.js storefront for a Medusa commerce backend. It renders the catalog, cart and checkout against the Store API, and is customized in TypeScript like any other Next.js application.

notes.text: A reachable Medusa backend is a precondition, not an option. Export MEDUSA_BACKEND_URL and MEDUSA_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (and optionally MEDUSA_DEFAULT_REGION and STOREFRONT_BASE_URL) before running the script and the storefront is built and started automatically. Without them the container is still fully installed, but the build is skipped.

Every setting is a NEXT_PUBLIC_ value, which Next inlines into the bundle at build time. After editing .env you must run medusajs-storefront-rebuild; restarting the service alone keeps serving the old values, which looks exactly like the change not taking effect.

The backend's STORE_CORS must name this storefront's origin, and AUTH_CORS too if customer accounts are used. The browser calls the backend directly, so without it every request is blocked client-side and the storefront appears empty.
NEXT_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_REGION must name a region that exists in the backend. The Medusa starter seeds a Danish region by default, so a storefront pointed at 'us' shows nothing until a US region exists.
Updates bump the @medusajs packages and rebuild, leaving apps/storefront/src untouched so your customizations survive. The starter itself is never re-fetched.
